Net sales - Net sales are derived from the sale of our products and related freight charges, less discounts, rebates and returns.

For the year ended May 31, 2025, net sales decreased $11.4 million to $292.5 million compared to the year ended May 31, 2024. At May 31, 2025, the Company had a backlog of $0.3 million compared to $1.3 million at the end of May 31, 2024.

The Med Tech business net sales increased $20.3 million for the year ended May 31, 2025 compared to the prior year. The change in sales from the prior year was primarily driven by:

• Increased Auryon sales of $9.8 million;

• Decreased sales of Syntrax of $0.4 million due to the discontinuation of this product line as of February 29, 2024;

• Increased sales of the thrombus management platform of $10.9 million, which was driven by increases in AngioVac, AlphaVac and thrombolytic sales of $5.8 million, $4.0 million and $1.1 million, respectively; and

• NanoKnife sales remained consistent year over year, and was comprised of increased NanoKnife disposable sales of $1.7 million offset by decreased capital sales of $1.7 million.

The Med Device business net sales decreased $31.7 million for the year ended May 31, 2025 compared to the prior year. The backlog, which primarily impacted sales of Core and Vascular Access products, was $0.3 million at May 31, 2025 compared to $1.3 million at May 31, 2024.

intro.text: AngioDynamics is a dynamic, diversified medical technology company committed to expanding treatment options and improving patient outcomes and quality of life by designing, manufacturing and selling products and technologies which aid clinicians in the treatment of patients with cardiovascular disease and cancer diagnoses. Our execution strategy is built on innovative R&D, clinical and regulatory pathway expansion and customer centric sales performance. AngioDynamics was founded in Queensbury, N.Y., U.S., in 1988 and began manufacturing and shipping product in the early 1990s. The Company is headquartered in Latham, N.Y., with manufacturing primarily out of the Queensbury facility.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Long-term debt (incl. current portion)
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans, current maturities included: financial.

lines.name: Finance lease liabilities
lines.why: Leases that work like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
